property_summary: For any nonzero ETH deposit sent to C via its receive() by any sender, the contract's public depositsCount increases by 1 (the buggy mutant reverts/prevents increment and thus can violate this for some deposits).

For any external sender sending a nonzero ETH value to C via its receive(), the contract's public depositsCount increases by 1 (the mutant's always-failing require prevents the increment and thus violates this for some deposit amounts and senders).

For every sender and nonzero ETH amount sent to C via its receive(), the public depositsCount increases by exactly 1 (the mutant's receive() always reverts, so for some admissible deposits the call will fail and depositsCount will not increase).

For every successful receive() call, depositsCount in the reference C is non-decreasing (it never wraps/decreases because the contract checks that depositsCount+1 >= depositsCount); removing that check can allow a wrap/overflow-like decrease in depositsCount for some maliciously crafted sequence of calls/inputs.

For every single payable receive call that completes successfully, the contract's depositsCount is non-decreasing (i.e., each successful receive yields depositsCount' >= depositsCount); the mutant removes the safety check so a reentrant attacker can cause depositsCount to increase twice within one outer receive and thereby make it observable that the post-call depositsCount differs from the expected non-decreasing behavior.

For any single external send to the contract's receive() with any sender and any value, the reference C increments depositsCount at most once per top-level receive call (so after the call depositsCount == old+1), but the mutant (without the require) can be reentered by a malicious recipient causing depositsCount to increase more than once during a single top-level receive, violating the one-increment-per-receive property.

For any single external top-level transfer into C (one call to receive), the reference guarantees depositsCount increases by exactly 1 after the call; the mutant (without the require) can be exploited by a reentrant attacker to make depositsCount increase by more than 1 during a single top-level receive, breaking this rule.

For every single external payable call that triggers C.receive, the reference C guarantees depositsCount increases by exactly 1 after the top-level call returns; removing the require allows a reentrant attacker to cause depositsCount to increase by more than 1 during a single top-level receive, which the mutant can exhibit.

For any nonzero ETH sent to C.receive, the reference contract always increments depositsCount by 1 (so depositsCount_after == depositsCount_before + 1); the mutant blocks the increment (requires overflow), so for some fuzzed payment amounts the mutant will not increase depositsCount and thus violates the rule.

For any nonzero ETH sent to C via its receive(), the reference contract always increments depositsCount by exactly 1 (depositsCount_after == depositsCount_before + 1); the mutant inverts the require and can block the increment for some payments, violating this rule.

For any caller sending a nonzero ETH value to C.receive(), the reference contract always increases depositsCount by 1; the mutant blocks the increment for some payable calls, causing depositsCount to not increase.

For any externally-sent nonzero Ether payment to C via its receive() the reference increases depositsCount by exactly 1 (depositsCount_after == depositsCount_before + 1); the mutant's inverted require can prevent the increment for some payments, breaking this rule.

For any nonzero ETH sent to C via its receive() by any sender, the reference increments depositsCount by exactly 1 (depositsCount_after == depositsCount_before + 1); the mutant's inverted require can block the increment for some nonzero payments, violating this rule.

For any received payment that does not revert, the reference contract increments depositsCount exactly once per successful receive call (so depositsCount after a receive is >= previous value and never increases when receive reverts); the mutant increments depositsCount before the safety check causing depositsCount to increase even when the receive should be rejected, so there exist inputs where depositsCount is larger in the mutant than in the reference.

For any call to receive that the reference contract accepts, depositsCount never increases when the call would have been rejected; the mutant increments depositsCount even when the receive should be rejected, so there exist inputs (sender with failing fallback) where depositsCount increases in the mutant but not in the reference.

For any call to receive() with any sender and any value, the reference contract never increases depositsCount when the receive call reverts; the mutant can increment depositsCount even when the receive call reverts (i.e. depositsCount only increases on successful receives in the reference, but the mutant may increase it on failing receives).

For any external low-level call target that reverts, the correct contract never increments depositsCount when the call fails, whereas the mutant increments depositsCount even if the external call reverts (so depositsCount remains unchanged on a failing callee in the reference but can increase in the mutant).

For every call to receive with any msg.value and sender, the reference C preserves the invariant that depositsCount after the call is >= depositsCount before the call and that the increment only happens at most once per successful receive; the mutant can increase depositsCount even when the safety check would have previously prevented the state change (so there exists a sender/value where depositsCount(final) == depositsCount(initial) for the reference but > for the mutant).
Only the owner can successfully withdraw the contract's balance via withdrawAll (i.e., withdrawAll reverts for non-owner callers).
Calling withdrawAll should succeed when msg.sender is the contract owner and revert for non-owners (i.e., onlyOwner enforces msg.sender == owner).

Invariant: only the deployer (owner) can cause the contract's balance to become zero via withdrawAll — the reference C preserves that for every caller, but the mutant removing onlyOwner allows a non-owner caller to drain the contract for some inputs (fuzzer will find a non-owner caller and nonzero balance).

For every caller, calling withdrawAll does not change the contract balance unless the caller is the owner; the mutant that removes onlyOwner allows a non-owner caller to drain the contract (change address(c).balance) for some inputs.

For every caller, invoking withdrawAll never makes the contract balance decrease unless that caller is the owner; the mutant removing onlyOwner allows a non-owner caller to cause the contract balance to drop for some inputs (a nonzero contract balance and a non-owner caller).

For every caller and for every nonzero contract balance funded by ANY address, calling withdrawAll either succeeds only when the caller is the owner (reference) — equivalently, after a non-owner calls withdrawAll the contract balance remains equal to the pre-call balance in the reference; the mutant removes the owner guard so there exists a caller and funding amount for which a non-owner call to withdrawAll reduces address(c).balance (i.e. the contract gets drained).

For every caller and any funding amount, if a non-owner calls withdrawAll the reference contract never transfers out the contract balance (address(c).balance remains equal before and after); the mutant that removes onlyOwner allows some non-owner caller and funding amount to make address(c).balance decrease (i.e., drain the contract).

After depositing some ether, a withdraw call by owner always decreases the contract balance by exactly the withdrawn amount (i.e., transfer never fails silently), so address(c).balance_after == address(c).balance_before - amount.

property_summary: For the owner calling withdraw with any uint amount, the call does not revert (i.e., withdraw always succeeds).
Calling c.withdraw(amount) from InvMutTest.run must not revert (reverted == false).
Calling withdraw(amount) on c from the test should not revert (reverted == false).
When InvMutTest.run is called by the owner with address(c).balance >= amount, calling c.withdraw(amount) must not revert (i.e., reverted == false).

For any target and value, if a call to sendMoney(target, value) succeeds (does not revert) then the contract C's balance decreases by exactly `value` (i.e., funds forwarded out are not silently dropped); replacing transfer with send that returns false can cause the call to succeed while funds are not forwarded, breaking this invariant.

For any recipient contract that either accepts or rejects ether, calling sendMoney(recipient, amt) from owner always results in the same change to C's balance for the correct contract (transfer either forwards and reverts on failure), while the mutant using .send may silently fail to forward funds (returning false) and thus leaves C's balance larger for some recipient/amount — the reference never silently accepts failed sends, the mutant can.

For any recipient contract that reverts in its fallback/receive, the reference C's sendMoney call (which uses transfer) always reverts (so the call to sendMoney fails), while the mutant using send will not revert but instead return false causing sendMoney to succeed — so the property's: 'sendMoney to a reverting recipient always reverts' holds for the reference but is broken by the mutant.

For any recipient contract that reverts when receiving ether, the reference C's sendMoney(address,uint) call (which uses .call in sendMoney but withdraw uses transfer elsewhere) does not allow the owner to later withdraw funds via withdraw(uint) failing due to lost balance — specifically, after a failing external send via sendMoney the contract's withdraw(uint) using transfer still forwards funds to owner (i.e., owner can always withdraw up to address(c).balance); the mutant that changes withdraw to use .send may have withdraw(uint) fail (return false) and thus revert, preventing the owner from retrieving contract balance for some fuzzed payment amounts and adversarial recipient behavior.

For any recipient contract and any amount, if the owner funds C and then calls sendMoney(recipient, amt) which causes the recipient to accept or reject the incoming Ether, the owner must always be able to withdraw the full remaining balance of C afterwards using withdraw(uint) (i.e., withdraw(address(c).balance) always succeeds in the reference), but the mutant that replaces transfer with send in withdraw can fail to forward Ether to the owner (returning false) and thus revert, breaking this guarantee for some recipient/amount.

Only the original owner can cause a reduction of the contract's balance via withdraw — after calling withdraw with any amount, the contract balance is <= its previous balance only if the caller is the owner.

property_summary: For any caller and any value, withdraw(...) invoked by the owner either reverts on failure to send (reference uses transfer which reverts on failure) or, equivalently, the reference never silently fails to transfer funds to the owner — i.e., when withdraw is called by owner with a value greater than contract balance or when the recipient's fallback reverts, the reference call to withdraw will revert, but the mutant using unchecked call may return successfully while leaving contract balance unchanged.

For any caller and any target that reverts on receiving Ether, when the owner calls withdraw(amount) the correct contract always reverts (so the contract balance remains unchanged), whereas the mutant using unchecked call may not revert and thus can leave the contract balance decreased unexpectedly.

For any amount and any recipient contract that reverts on receiving Ether, the reference contract's withdraw(amount) (which uses transfer) always reverts when the recipient's fallback/receive reverts, so the call does not succeed; the mutant (using unchecked call) can return successfully despite the recipient reverting, violating that property for some inputs.
